## Historical audit: S0123

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 1 of 2 is available; citations below refer to its JSONL lines.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal: student `model_request`, line 1 | Reconstruct a single indoor photograph as editable SceneAct meshes, matching camera, colors, proportions and occlusions. The student’s “ship accommodation” interpretation and image anchors are estimates, not independently verified scene identity (student `model_response`, line 3). |
| Initial build: student `model_response` line 3; `execute` line 4 | The program constructs multiple grouped objects: architecture, bunks, cabinets, lockers, chair, machine, pipes, fittings and lamps. Composite parts are positioned using explicit coordinates and grouped with `include`; grouping alone does not verify physical connections. It specifies colored surfaces, a camera and lights; no texture maps are evident in the code. |
| First validation: `execution_result` line 5; student request line 8 | Step 1 returned `ok: true` and logged a saved render and blend file. The next request supplied the render and asked for comparison; this is operational validation, not independent visual or geometric verification. |
| Autonomous revision: student `model_response` line 10; `execute` line 11 | The student diagnosed excessive brightness, a column too far right and foreground bunk occlusion. The executed revision darkened lighting and colors, moved the column, removed the nearer bunk set, raised lockers, reoriented fittings and rotated the chair 12 degrees. It retained the camera and added roughness and emission adjustments. These are the student’s diagnoses, not verified defects. |
| Further revision: student `model_response` line 17; `execute` line 18 | After another render was supplied, the student judged furniture and fittings too low and the deck too orange. It raised bunk tiers, furniture, column paint division, fittings and lamps, and changed deck color. Pose and connections are specified in code but not independently checked. |
| Outcomes: `execution_result` lines 12 and 19; `select` lines 13–14 and 20–21 | Steps 2 and 3 also returned `ok: true` and logged saved renders. Step 3 was selected in the visible trace. The logs show 16 render samples despite 32 specified in the programs; the reason is not established. |

**Teacher input and adoption:** No teacher message, teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-directed execution appears in this visible chunk. The comparison prompts are harness/user feedback, and the subsequent code demonstrates student response to those prompts—not adoption of unseen teacher advice. Student CLI sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2, 9 and 16); the observed exploration was iterative program generation and runner feedback, not filesystem or external search.

**Assessment and uncertainty:** Three builds formally executed successfully; overall reconstruction correctness and final outcome remain unknown because neither images nor chunk 2 are visible. In particular, visual fidelity, actual part contact, material appearance, occlusion, camera framing and whether the lighting revisions improved the result cannot be verified. No visible execution failure or technical interruption is reported. A transferable observation is that render feedback supported targeted revisions; the particular column, bunk and illumination hypotheses are task-specific and remain unverified.
